purpose: Validate admission control, queue ordering, lifecycle accounting, and retry behavior without provider calls.
provenance: Synthetic workloads derived from the public AgentScheduler submit lifecycle and ResourceManager limits.
limitations: Does not measure LLM quality, provider latency, or production throughput.
Persistence and recovery adapters are stubbed by the runner.
Timing assertions are limited to ordering and resource ceilings for repeatability.

cases.description: Nine jobs across three tasks should honor global and per-task slot limits.
When one slot opens, the queued higher-priority job should start first.
An estimate larger than the token budget should be rejected without running.
A task that has consumed its cumulative token budget should block its next step.
A runner exception should be surfaced and counted as a failed job.
A cooperative checkpoint should requeue and execute the runner again.
A transient provider rate-limit error should requeue once and complete on retry.
